description.narrative:
Project Outcome: Environmental effects: The Project will support Argentinas efforts to reduce GHG emissions by enabling greater use of renewable energy in an energy matrix still dominated by fossil fuels, and energy-related CO2 emissions. Aligned with the governments commitment to cap emissions and reach Net Zero by 2050, the Project contributes through a 150 MW BESS that will enhance grid flexibility and enable the reliable integration of intermittent renewable generation, together with the acquisition of the shares of the hydropower plant expected to improve operational efficiency. The sponsor, Argentinas largest private generator with 6.7 GW across thermal, hydro, wind, solar, provides strong operational capacity and extensive experience in a challenging macroeconomic context.
Market Creation Outcome: Sustainability: The Project will strengthen the sustainability of Argentinas power sector by demonstrating the countrys first utility-scale BESSa critical enabler of renewable integration at a time when transmission bottlenecks, wind curtailment, and climate-driven hydrological variability constrain clean-energy expansion. With natural gas representing almost half of domestic generation and persistent grid congestion, the Project complements reforms under RenovAr and MATER and supports the governments target of 30% renewables by 2030. By supporting the 150 MW Puerto Nuevo BESSthe largest project awarded in the 2025 AlmaGBA auctionthe Project is expected to catalyze further private investment in storage and enhance grid reliability, reinforcing the replicability of the model as over 600 MW of additional BESS capacity advances toward commissioning.

The proposed investment consists of a senior unsecured corporate loan of up to US$ 300 million to Central Puerto S.A. (CEPU or the Company), comprising US$ 50 million from IFCs own account and US$ 250 million mobilized through B Loans from commercial and institutional lenders, to support two flagship investments under the Companys capital expenditure program: (i) the acquisition of the shares of the special purpose vehicle (SPV) that holds the new 30-year concession for the Piedra del Águila hydropower facility in Neuquén Province, as part of Argentinas initiative to re-privatize strategic hydroelectric assets; and (ii) the development of a 150 MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) at the Puerto Nuevo complex in Buenos Aires, the countrys first large-scale storage project (the Project).
